title: Optimizing Personal Financial Management with Hybrid AI: Integrating Sentiment Analysis and Fuzzy Logic for Dynamic Financial Planning
authors: Asemi, A.; Miah, M.J.; Asemi, M.
venue: Journal of Economics, Finance and Management Studies
tldr: A hybrid AI system integrating NLP sentiment analysis with fuzzy logic dynamically adjusts financial recommendations based on both market conditions and user emotional states.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional PFM systems rely on static rules that fail to adapt to changing market conditions or individual emotional states affecting financial decisions. Users often receive generic advice that does not account for behavioral patterns, emotional influences, or real-time market sentiment.
approach: Developed a hybrid AI system integrating NLP sentiment analysis with fuzzy logic for financial planning.
Created a simulated user interaction dataset with behavioral patterns, spending habits, and financial goals.
Implemented sentiment analysis using NLP to process user communications and market news.
Applied fuzzy logic to model uncertainty in both market conditions and user emotional states.
Generated personalized, real-time financial recommendations based on combined sentiment and market analysis.
Conducted comprehensive performance evaluation with 10,000 test cases.
findings: num: 95% accuracy in sentiment detection across positive, neutral, and negative categories.
num: Average time savings of 35% compared to manual financial analysis.
num: 18% improvement in financial decision outcomes.
The hybrid system effectively balances objective market data with subjective emotional factors.
key_figures_tables: Table 1: Dataset features including 12 variables: demographics, financial status, transaction history, and financial goals.
Table 2: Sentiment classification results with 95.2% accuracy, 93.5% recall, and 94.3% F1-score.
Table 3: Fuzzy logic rule system with inputs (Market Trend, Risk Tolerance, Sentiment Score) and outputs (Recommendation Type, Risk Level, Amount).
Table 4: Comprehensive performance evaluation showing system accuracy, user satisfaction, and financial outcome improvements.

key_equations.equation: Fuzzy Rule: IF Market is Strong AND Risk is Moderate AND Sentiment is Positive THEN Recommend Balanced Portfolio
key_equations.explanation: Example fuzzy logic rule combining market conditions, risk tolerance, and sentiment analysis for investment recommendations.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper presents a novel hybrid AI system combining NLP sentiment analysis with fuzzy logic for personalized financial planning. It demonstrates that accounting for user emotional states alongside market conditions produces more effective financial recommendations than traditional static approaches. The 95% sentiment detection accuracy and 18% improvement in financial outcomes validate the approach.
directly_justifies: Combining sentiment analysis with fuzzy logic improves financial recommendation accuracy.
User emotional states are significant factors in financial decision-making that should be considered.
Hybrid AI systems can adapt recommendations based on real-time market and emotional conditions.
limits: Uses simulated data rather than real user financial data.
Fuzzy logic rules are manually defined rather than learned from data.
95% accuracy achieved on controlled test cases; real-world performance may differ.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 3 (Psychology of Personal Finance) is highly relevant through 3.A (Cognitive Biases in Financial Decisions) as the system accounts for emotional influences. Domain 7 (Budgeting Strategies) is highly relevant through both 7.B (AI and LLM-Based Analysis) and 7.C (Constrained Optimization). Domain 10 (Privacy) partially applies through 10.A regarding handling of emotional data. Other domains like 1-2, 4-6, 8-9, 11-14 are less directly applicable.

limitations: Relies on simulated user interaction data rather than real-world financial records.
Fuzzy logic rules are manually defined, limiting scalability and adaptability.
Single-sentiment model approach may not capture all emotional nuances.
Limited to financial recommendations; does not integrate with actual banking systems.
